question: Which of the following reactions is an example of a precipitation reaction?
solution:
The correct answer is __**AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO3**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **precipitation reaction** is a type of chemical reaction in which **two soluble salts** in aqueous solution combine to form one or more **insoluble products**, called a **precipitate**.
 
• In the reaction **AgNO3 + NaCl → AgCl↓ + NaNO3**, aqueous **Silver Nitrate** reacts with aqueous **Sodium Chloride** to form **Silver Chloride** and **Sodium Nitrate**. The **Silver Chloride (AgCl)** is insoluble in water and settles down as a **white precipitate**. ***Hence, option 1 is correct.***
 
• This reaction is also a classic example of a **double displacement reaction**, where the **Silver (Ag+)** and **Sodium (Na+)** cations exchange their respective **Nitrate (NO3-)** and **Chloride (Cl-)** anions.
 
• The **downward arrow (↓)** next to a chemical formula in an equation specifically denotes the formation of a **precipitate**, indicating that the substance has crashed out of the solution as a **solid**.
 
• Precipitation reactions are essential in **qualitative inorganic analysis** to identify various **ions** present in a solution based on the **color** and **solubility** of the precipitate formed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Decomposition Reaction:**

 
 
• In the reaction **CaCO3 → CaO + CO2↑**, **Calcium Carbonate** (limestone) breaks down into **Calcium Oxide** (quicklime) and **Carbon Dioxide** gas upon heating.
 
• This is a **thermal decomposition reaction**. The **upward arrow (↑)** indicates the evolution of a **gas**. ***Hence, option 2 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Single Displacement Reaction:**
 
 
• The reaction **Zn + H2SO4 → ZnSO4 + H2↑** involves **Zinc** metal reacting with **Sulfuric Acid**.
 
• Since **Zinc** is more reactive than **Hydrogen**, it displaces hydrogen from the acid to form **Zinc Sulfate** and **Hydrogen gas**. ***Hence, option 3 is incorrect.***
 
 
 
• **Neutralization Reaction:**
 
 
• The reaction **NaOH + HCl → NaCl + H2O** is a **neutralization reaction** occurring between a **strong base (Sodium Hydroxide)** and a **strong acid (Hydrochloric Acid)**.
 
• The products are **Sodium Chloride** (a soluble salt) and **Water**. No precipitate is formed in this specific reaction as all products remain in the aqueous phase or as liquid water. ***Hence, option 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Solubility Rules:** To predict whether a precipitation reaction will occur, chemists use **solubility rules**. For example, most **Nitrates (NO3-)** are **soluble**, while most **Silver salts** (except nitrates and fluorides) are **insoluble**.
 
• **Applications:** Precipitation reactions are used in **wastewater treatment** to remove **heavy metals** or **phosphates** from water by turning them into solid precipitates that can be easily filtered out.
 
• **Ionic Equation:** The **net ionic equation** for the correct answer is **Ag+(aq) + Cl-(aq) → AgCl(s)**, which focuses only on the species that actually change during the reaction.
 
• **Identification:** **Silver Chloride** is a **white** precipitate, **Silver Bromide** is **pale yellow**, and **Silver Iodide** is **bright yellow**. These distinct colors help in identifying **halide ions**.
